descriptionChirho: The primary Piel sense of דבר I: to speak, say, tell, declare, converse — covering all finite forms, infinitives, imperatives, and participles of the Piel stem where the meaning is active verbal communication, confirmed by the consistent Arabic cognate تَكَلَّمَ (takallama) across nearly all occurrences.

The Qal active participle of דבר I used substantivally: the speaker, one who speaks, the one speaking — Arabic المُتَكَلِّمُ (al-mutakallim, 'the speaker') confirms the agentive/substantive usage distinct from the Piel verbal action.
The Niphal stem of דבר I indicating reciprocal or reflexive speech: to speak with one another, to converse — Arabic تَكَلَّمُوا confirms mutual/reflexive speaking rather than directed speech.

The Hitpael reflexive-iterative stem of דבר I: to speak (with reflexive or intensive nuance), often rendered as ongoing or self-directed speech — Arabic مُتَكَلِّمًا (mutakalliman, active participle) confirms reflexive speaking.
The Pual passive stem of דבר I: to be spoken, to be said — Arabic يُتَحَدَّثُ (yutaḥaddathu, passive 'be spoken about') and مَقُولَة (maqūla, 'something said') confirm the passive voice meaning.

The Hifil causative stem of דבר II (a distinct homonymous root): to subdue, bring into subjection — Arabic يُخْضِعُ (yukhḍiʿu, 'he subdues') is the primary discriminator separating this from דבר I 'speak'; Korean 복종시키시도다 ('cause to submit') confirms.

The Piel of דבר II meaning to destroy or annihilate, related to דֶּבֶר (pestilence/plague) — Arabic وَأَبَادَتْ (wa-abādat, 'and she annihilated') and Swahili akawaangamiza ('destroyed them') confirm this is the destructive sense of the second root, not speech.
